observations.statement: catalog.chat_send maps cmd.chat.send to handlers::chat::send and declares chat.message.submitted as its expected event type.
cmd.chat.send availability and disabled copy are projected from named state paths, and its effect contract requires the declared event plus dispatch-correlation evidence.

The chat-send accessibility contract explicitly covers stable semantics, keyboard reachability and activation, deterministic focus after dispatch or error, and assistive-technology announcement of the disabled reason.
Settings, stop, message-detail toggle, web crawl, web extract, and web fetch are each mapped to a distinct command and handler while declaring no expected persisted event.
Each of the six no-event commands declares receipt effect_kind, states that no persisted event is declared, and names a command-specific dispatch_receipt reference.
The six no-event commands each require an event test that records a dispatch receipt or explicit no-persist route/open disposition and rejects unexpected persisted domain events.

Production certification for the generic no-event pattern requires render/control evidence, a dispatcher fixture, typed payload/result assertion, projected state and disabled-reason proof, receipt/event assertion, accessibility checking, and regression evidence.

The chat-send acceptance check requires trace preservation through result and receipt/event refs, while its named event test asserts the event with command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target.

candidate_findings.title: Chat-send schemas and validation semantics are not defined
candidate_findings.statement: The core requires cmd.chat.send to have typed payload, result, error, and UICommandResponse contracts, but it supplies no payload fields, result variants, error variants, validation constraints, or response mapping; its dispatcher fixture requirement reduces the oracle to a generic typed args/result contract.
candidate_findings.impact: Independent builders can create incompatible send contracts while satisfying the named checks, and message-input rejection and failure behavior cannot be certified from this window.

candidate_findings.title: Chat-send trace acceptance exceeds its concrete event oracle
candidate_findings.statement: The dispatch acceptance check requires preservation of result and receipt/event refs, but the concrete event test asserts only chat.message.submitted plus command_id, origin, correlation_id, and handler target.
candidate_findings.impact: A build could pass the named event test without proving that result or receipt/event references survive dispatch, weakening end-to-end traceability.

candidate_findings.title: Stop cancellation behavior is unspecified
candidate_findings.statement: The stop entry identifies cmd.chat.stop and its handler but otherwise permits a generic typed payload/result contract or route/open disposition and records only a no-persist receipt. It does not identify the generation, request, message, or session to stop, nor define cancellation timing, races, idempotency, partial-output handling, terminal result, or already-complete behavior.
candidate_findings.impact: Implementations can stop different scopes and resolve in-flight races differently while passing the dispatch and receipt checks, risking cancellation of the wrong work or misleading UI state.

candidate_findings.title: Message-detail toggle has no state-transition contract
candidate_findings.statement: cmd.chat.toggle_message_details has a handler and an availability selector, but its contract does not identify a target message, current detail state, resulting detail state, per-message versus global scope, persistence boundary, or repeated-toggle behavior; the declared effect is only a no-persist receipt or route/open disposition.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can implement incompatible toggle scope and state ownership, producing inconsistent visible details and untestable transition behavior.

candidate_findings.title: Crawl, extract, and fetch lack distinguishing operational contracts
candidate_findings.statement: Web crawl, extract, and fetch are routed to distinct handlers, but each uses the same generic typed payload/result-or-route/open requirement and the same no-persist receipt pattern. The window defines no command-specific inputs, outputs, validation rules, authorization checks, lifecycle, timeout, retry, cancellation, concurrency, or failure semantics that distinguish the operations.
candidate_findings.impact: Builders can choose incompatible URL, content, traversal, result, and failure behavior while certification proves only dispatch, availability, receipt, and accessibility plumbing.

candidate_findings.title: No-event effect representation admits incompatible alternatives
candidate_findings.statement: For each no-event command, effect_kind is receipt and receipt_or_event_refs names a dispatch_receipt, while the description and event test also permit a route/open disposition. The contract does not define selection criteria, a discriminator, or the required evidence shape when route/open is chosen.
candidate_findings.impact: Handlers and tests can encode materially different successful effects, and consumers cannot rely on one stable receipt/disposition representation.

candidate_findings.title: Availability projections have no state model
candidate_findings.statement: All seven entries name availability and disabled-reason projection paths, but the window does not define the availability value domain, transition triggers, disabled-reason precedence, atomicity between the two projections, or stale-state behavior during dispatch.
candidate_findings.impact: Controls can enable, disable, and announce reasons inconsistently even when they read the required paths.

candidate_findings.title: Settings destination and completion behavior are underdetermined
candidate_findings.statement: The settings entry maps cmd.chat.settings to handlers::chat::settings but does not identify the settings destination, navigation or modal behavior, initial section, completion result, or focus destination; its payload/result requirement can instead be satisfied by an unspecified route/open disposition.
candidate_findings.impact: Different settings surfaces and navigation outcomes can satisfy the same wiring evidence, leaving user-visible behavior and focus restoration non-deterministic.

candidate_findings.title: Non-send commands omit typed error and response contracts
candidate_findings.statement: Chat send explicitly requires typed error and UICommandResponse contracts, whereas settings, stop, toggle, crawl, extract, and fetch require only typed payload/result or route/open disposition even though their accessibility contracts contemplate dispatch errors.
candidate_findings.impact: Error classification, result-to-error mapping, user-visible failure handling, and dispatcher response compatibility can diverge across these commands without violating the stated acceptance checks.

explicit_non_gaps.statement: The send command's domain effect is explicit: chat.message.submitted is the expected event, and fabricated *.command_applied events are expressly invalid.
The chat-send control has an explicit four-part accessibility contract covering semantics, keyboard access, focus management, and disabled-state announcement.
The chat-send command-to-handler route and dispatcher reachability oracle are explicit.
No-event commands are explicitly forbidden from emitting unexpected persisted domain events and must leave a receipt or explicit no-persist route/open disposition.
The generic production-certification checklist explicitly spans rendering, dispatch, typing, state, disabled reason, effects, accessibility, and regression evidence.

unknowns.statement: The exact payload fields, result shape, error taxonomy, UICommandResponse mapping, and validation rules for cmd.chat.send are unknown within this window.
The target identity and post-cancellation state for cmd.chat.stop are unknown within this window.
Whether message details are per-message, per-thread, or global, and whether their state persists, is unknown within this window.
The input, output, validation, authorization, and lifecycle contracts for crawl, extract, and fetch are unknown within this window.
The rule selecting a dispatch receipt versus route/open disposition, and the evidence representation of the latter, is unknown within this window.
The availability value vocabulary, transition ordering, and disabled-reason precedence are unknown within this window.
